## Multiple Choice Questions

**1.** A transaction amount of $15,000 is recorded in the general ledger as $1,500 due to a data entry error. This is an example of a problem with which data quality dimension?

A.  Accuracy
B.  Completeness
C.  Consistency
D.  Timeliness

**2.** An auditor discovers that several hundred records in the Charles River Shipment table have no value in the TrackingNumber field, which nearly every other shipment carries. This situation represents a problem with which data quality dimension?

A.  Accuracy
B.  Completeness
C.  Consistency
D.  Timeliness

**3.** Some shipments in the Charles River Shipment table are marked "In Transit" in the Status column, although the DeliveryDate column, which records the date the goods arrived, shows a date years before the year-end under review. Which data quality dimension best describes the disagreement between the two columns?

A.  Accuracy
B.  Completeness
C.  Consistency
D.  Timeliness

**4.** Which of the following is an example of qualitative data in an accounting context?

A.  The name of the cost center to which an expense is assigned
B.  The total amount of a sales invoice
C.  The number of units of inventory on hand
D.  The gross profit margin expressed as a percentage

**5.** For an analysis in which each department-month is one observation, a budget spreadsheet with months as column headers (January, February, March) and departments as rows is considered "messy." Which tidy data principle does it violate?

A.  Each variable should occupy its own column
B.  Each observation should occupy its own row
C.  Each type of observational unit should form its own table
D.  Both A and B

**6.** An auditor performs analytical procedures using general ledger data extracted from the client's ERP system on March 11 for a fiscal year ending December 31. The final three adjusting entries for the year were posted on March 12, after the extract was taken. Which data quality dimension best describes the problem with the date of the extract?

A.  Accuracy
B.  Completeness
C.  Consistency
D.  Timeliness

**7.** Which of the following matches an accounting source with its data structure correctly?

A.  An XBRL filing is unstructured, because its data are not arranged in rows and columns.
B.  A scanned supplier invoice is structured, because the ERP system stores it as a file.
C.  A general ledger table is structured, and the narrative text of a contract is unstructured.
D.  A payroll register is semi-structured, because each row combines amounts with employee names.

**8.** A management accountant discovers that the same product appears in the Item table under two different ItemID values because it was entered separately by two warehouse locations. This is an example of which data quality problem?

A.  Duplicate record
B.  Missing value
C.  Outlier
D.  Timeliness problem

**9.** Which of the following sources of accounting data provides the most complete picture of an organization's financial transactions?

A.  The accounts receivable sub-ledger
B.  An external bank statement
C.  The general ledger
D.  A product inventory listing

**10.** In the Charles River dataset, the GLEntry table includes a SourceDocumentType column. Which of the following best describes the purpose of this column?

A.  It identifies the kind of document that created the entry, such as a sales invoice.
B.  It records the name of the employee who posted the entry to the ledger.
C.  It stores the total amount of the transaction as text rather than as a number.
D.  It indicates whether a supervisor approved the entry before it was posted.

**11.** A dataset is organized so that each variable occupies its own column and each observation occupies its own row, but several records contain data entry errors in the amount field. This dataset is best described as:

A.  Tidy and clean
B.  Tidy but not clean
C.  Clean but not tidy
D.  Neither tidy nor clean

**12.** A financial analyst summarizes Charles River revenue by customer name instead of by CustomerID. Two customers with different CustomerIDs, one located in Moniqueborough and one in Kingfurt, appear in the summary as a single line labeled "Brown LLC." What caused this result?

A.  The PivotTable or query contains an error in its formulas.
B.  One of the two customers was never entered into the Customer table.
C.  Grouping by name combined two different customers that share the same name.
D.  The Customer table is more current than the sales data.

**13.** An enterprise resource planning system is distinct from a standalone accounting package primarily because an ERP system:

A.  Uses a relational database to store its accounting and operating data
B.  Integrates sales, production, purchasing, and human resources data in one database
C.  Produces the financial statements automatically at the end of each period
D.  Eliminates all data quality problems through built-in validation rules

**14.** Which of the following best explains why data quality assessment should be performed before any analysis begins?

A.  Analytical software cannot open or process data that contains quality problems.
B.  Professional standards prohibit accountants from using any data that contains missing values.
C.  Data quality assessment is required only for audits, not for managerial or financial reporting work.
D.  Quality problems can make results unreliable, and finding them first lets the accountant address them.

**15.** An auditor examining the Charles River GLEntry table uses the SourceDocumentType column to separate entries generated by SalesInvoice from entries generated by JournalEntry. This separation is most useful for which audit procedure?

A.  Calculating the total revenue for the period from the sales postings
B.  Selecting the journal entries to test for management override of controls
C.  Verifying that the general ledger is stored in a tidy data format
D.  Confirming that every customer in the Customer table has placed an order
